worked.title: Q1 · PCA after scaling the features; SVM dual in two variables (16 marks)

problem.text: (a) PCA on N > 10000 mean-centred points in D > 100 dimensions gave the top 10 principal components. Every point (x₁, …, x_D) must now be changed to (α₁x₁, …, α_Dx_D) for fixed constants αᵢ. The data scientist says he can just change each eigenvector (b₁, …, b_D) to (α₁b₁, …, α_Db_D). Is he right? [5M]  (b) He has the old covariance matrix. Can he get the covariance matrix of the scaled data in O(D²) time? [3M]  (c) Points (x, y, class): (−1, 3, +), (1, 3, −), (−1, 1, −). With multipliers αᵢ, write the SVM dual objective as a polynomial in the fewest variables and terms, and find the optimal hyperplane wᵀx + b = 0 by calculus. [8M]

steps.label: What is tested
steps.text: (a)–(b) how scaling the features changes the covariance matrix and its eigenvectors (PCA). (c) building and solving the hard-margin SVM dual by hand. Marks: 5 + 3 + 8.

steps.label: Notation
steps.text: This paper's symbols: **X** = D × N data matrix (one column per point), **R** = diag(α₁, …, α_D) = the scaling, **S Λ Sᵀ** = the old covariance's eigendecomposition. In (a)–(b) the αᵢ are **scaling constants**, not step sizes. In (c) the αᵢ are the **SVM dual multipliers** (one per point).

steps.label: (a) STEP 1 · Write the change as a matrix
steps.text:
Scaling every point = multiplying by the diagonal matrix R:
x ↦ Rx, so X ↦ RX

steps.label: (a) STEP 2 · New covariance  [3M]
steps.text:
Old covariance (mean-centred): XXᵀ = SΛSᵀ (spectral theorem)
New covariance: (RX)(RX)ᵀ = R XXᵀ Rᵀ = R SΛSᵀ R
It looks like an eigendecomposition with eigenvector matrix RS …

steps.label: (a) STEP 3 · Why he is wrong  [2M]
steps.text:
… but an eigenvector matrix must be **orthogonal**:
(RS)(RS)ᵀ = R SSᵀ R = R² ≠ I (unless every αᵢ = ±1)
So RSΛSᵀR is **not** an eigendecomposition, and the columns Rbᵢ are not the new principal directions.
Small check: S = [[2, 1], [1, 2]] has PCs (1, 1) and (1, −1). Scale by R = diag(1, 2): his vectors are (1, 2) and (1, −2), whose dot product is 1 − 4 = −3 ≠ 0. Principal directions are always perpendicular, so these cannot be them.
**He is wrong.**

steps.label: (b) STEP 4 · New covariance from the old one  [2M]
steps.text:
New covariance = R(XXᵀ)R, and XXᵀ is already known.
R is diagonal, so entry (i, j) is just
(R XXᵀ R)ᵢⱼ = αᵢ (XXᵀ)ᵢⱼ αⱼ

steps.label: (b) STEP 5 · Count the work  [1M]
steps.text:
D × D = D² entries, each needs 2 multiplications ⇒ **O(D²)** time.
(The key says the same with columns: multiplying by a diagonal matrix scales each column or row, O(D) per column, O(D²) in total.)
**Yes, he is justified.**

steps.label: (c) STEP 7 · Dual objective  [3M]
steps.text:
L = α₁ + α₂ + α₃ − ½ΣᵢΣⱼ αᵢαⱼyᵢyⱼ xᵢ·xⱼ
= α₁ + α₂ + α₃ − ½[10α₁² + 10α₂² + 2α₃² + 2α₁α₂(−1)(8) + 2α₁α₃(−1)(4) + 2α₂α₃(+1)(2)]
subject to α₁y₁ + α₂y₂ + α₃y₃ = 0 and αᵢ ≥ 0

steps.label: (c) STEP 8 · Fewest variables  [2M]
steps.text:
Constraint: α₁ − α₂ − α₃ = 0 ⇒ α₁ = α₂ + α₃
Substitute and collect (the α₂α₃ terms cancel):
L = **2α₂ + 2α₃ − 2α₂² − 2α₃²**
Two variables, four terms.

steps.label: Answers at a glance
steps.text: (a) Wrong: RS is not orthogonal, so Rbᵢ are not the new PCs. (b) Yes: αᵢSᵢⱼαⱼ, O(D²). (c) L = 2α₂ + 2α₃ − 2α₂² − 2α₃²; α = (1, 0.5, 0.5); −x₁ + x₂ − 3 = 0.

steps.label: Where marks are lost
steps.text:
• (a) Saying "yes" because R SΛSᵀ R looks like a decomposition, without checking orthogonality.
• (c) Forgetting the yᵢyⱼ signs, or not using Σαᵢyᵢ = 0 to remove a variable.
• (c) Finding b from a point that is not a support vector.

steps.label: More
steps.text: (c) in full: [Lecture 15, Dual tab](#/sem1/aiml-zc416/ch15/f-dual/2).

worked.title: Q2 · Convexity proofs; SVD and the trace; gradients of quadratic forms (12 marks)

problem.text: (a) Prove or disprove: (i) f₁(x) = ‖x‖₁ is convex (norm properties); (ii) if g is convex, h(x) = g(Ax + b) is convex (definition). [4M]  (b) A = UΣVᵀ, ‖Σ‖²_F = γ, B = AᵀA, α = B₁₁ + … + Bₙₙ. Prove or disprove: (a) G1: α = γ; (b) G2: α = √γ; (c) with C = AAᵀ and β = its trace, β = γ². [4M]  (c) f(x) = ‖Ax − b‖²₂ + cᵀx + d and g(x) = ‖A₁ᵀA₁x‖²₂ + ‖A₂ᵀx‖²₂. Derive ∇f and ∇g. [4M]

steps.label: What is tested
steps.text: (a) convexity from the definition [4M]. (b) trace and Frobenius norm through the SVD [4M]. (c) the rule ∇(xᵀMx) = (M + Mᵀ)x [4M].

steps.label: Notation
steps.text: This paper's symbols are kept: σᵢ = singular values (the diagonal of Σ), tr = trace (sum of the diagonal). In (a) the key's λ is the mixing weight (θ on the slides).

steps.label: (a) STEP 1 · Both convex
steps.text:
(i) ‖λx + (1 − λ)y‖₁ ≤ ‖λx‖₁ + ‖(1 − λ)y‖₁ (triangle inequality) [1M] = λ‖x‖₁ + (1 − λ)‖y‖₁ (homogeneity, λ ≥ 0) [0.5M] ⇒ convex [0.5M].
(ii) h(λx + (1 − λ)y) = g(λ(Ax + b) + (1 − λ)(Ay + b)) (write b = λb + (1 − λ)b) ≤ λg(Ax + b) + (1 − λ)g(Ay + b) = λh(x) + (1 − λ)h(y) ⇒ convex [2M].

steps.label: (b) STEP 2 · γ in terms of σ  [0.5M]
steps.text: ‖Σ‖²_F = sum of squares of all entries = **σ₁² + σ₂² + … + σₙ² = γ**

steps.label: (b) STEP 3 · α = tr(AᵀA)  [0.5M]
steps.text:
AᵀA = VΣᵀUᵀUΣVᵀ = VΣᵀΣVᵀ   (UᵀU = I)
tr(AᵀA) = tr(VΣᵀΣVᵀ) = tr(ΣᵀΣVᵀV) = tr(ΣᵀΣ)   (tr(MN) = tr(NM), VᵀV = I)
= σ₁² + … + σₙ² = **γ**

steps.label: (b) STEP 4 · Verdicts
steps.text:
G1 (α = γ): **true** [1M].
G2 (α = √γ): **false** in general, since α = γ (equal only when γ = 0 or 1) [1M].
β = tr(AAᵀ) = tr(UΣΣᵀUᵀ) = tr(ΣΣᵀ) = γ, so **β = γ² is false** (unless γ = 0 or 1) [1.5M].

steps.label: (c) STEP 5 · ∇f  [2M]
steps.text:
‖Ax − b‖² = (Ax − b)ᵀ(Ax − b) = xᵀAᵀAx − 2bᵀAx + bᵀb [1M]
∇(xᵀAᵀAx) = 2AᵀAx (AᵀA is symmetric), ∇(2bᵀAx) = 2Aᵀb [0.5M]
∇(cᵀx + d) = c [0.5M]
**∇f = 2AᵀAx − 2Aᵀb + c**

steps.label: (c) STEP 6 · ∇g  [2M]
steps.text:
‖A₁ᵀA₁x‖² = xᵀ(A₁ᵀA₁)ᵀ(A₁ᵀA₁)x = xᵀA₁ᵀA₁A₁ᵀA₁x [0.5M] ⇒ gradient 2A₁ᵀA₁A₁ᵀA₁x [0.5M]
‖A₂ᵀx‖² = xᵀA₂A₂ᵀx [0.5M] ⇒ gradient 2A₂A₂ᵀx [0.5M]
**∇g = 2A₁ᵀA₁A₁ᵀA₁x + 2A₂A₂ᵀx**

steps.label: Answers at a glance
steps.text: (a) Both convex. (b) G1 true; G2 false; β = γ, so β = γ² false. (c) ∇f = 2AᵀAx − 2Aᵀb + c; ∇g = 2A₁ᵀA₁A₁ᵀA₁x + 2A₂A₂ᵀx.

steps.label: Where marks are lost
steps.text:
• (b) Forgetting tr(MN) = tr(NM), or that UᵀU = VᵀV = I.
• (c) Writing 2Mx when M is not symmetric (here every M is symmetric, so 2Mx is fine; say so).
• (c) Dropping the −2Aᵀb cross term.

steps.label: More
steps.text: (a) in full: [Lecture 11, Convexity tab](#/sem1/aiml-zc416/ch11/f-convex/19).

worked.answer: (a) Both convex. (b) α = γ (G1 right, G2 wrong), β = γ ≠ γ². (c) ∇f = 2AᵀAx − 2Aᵀb + c; ∇g = 2A₁ᵀA₁A₁ᵀA₁x + 2A₂A₂ᵀx.

worked.title: Q3 · Inner product from a matrix; linear approximation; nearest zero-trace matrix (12 marks)

problem.text: (a) A = [[1, 0, ρ], [0, 1, ρ], [ρ, ρ, 1]]. (i) For which ρ is ⟨x, y⟩_A = xᵀAy an inner product on ℝ³? [3M] (ii) Is x = (1, 0, 0) perpendicular to y = (0, 1, 0) under it? Find all z perpendicular to both. [3M]  (b) f(x) = [xᵀQx, bᵀx]ᵀ, Q 3 × 3 symmetric positive definite, x, b ∈ ℝ³. (i) ∇ₓf. [1M] (ii) Linear approximation of f about (0, 0, 0). [2M]  (c) Find a 2 × 2 matrix M with trace(M) = 0 minimising ‖M − A‖², A = [[1, 0], [0, 2]]. [3M]

steps.label: What is tested
steps.text: (a) an inner product needs A symmetric positive definite [6M]. (b) the Jacobian of a vector function and the first-order Taylor approximation [3M]. (c) Lagrange with one equality constraint [3M].

steps.label: Notation
steps.text: This paper's symbols are kept: ρ = an unknown number in A (not a forgetting factor). In (a)(i) λ = eigenvalue; in (c) λ = the equality multiplier (μ on the boards).

steps.label: (a)(i) STEP 1 · Eigenvalues  [2M]
steps.text:
A is symmetric, so it gives an inner product exactly when it is positive definite (all eigenvalues > 0).
det(A − λI) = (1 − λ)[(1 − λ)² − 2ρ²] = 0 [0.5M]
⇒ λ = 1, 1 + ρ√2, 1 − ρ√2 [1.5M]

steps.label: (a)(i) STEP 2 · Condition  [1M]
steps.text:
1 + ρ√2 > 0 and 1 − ρ√2 > 0 ⇒ **−1/√2 < ρ < 1/√2**
(Quicker check with leading minors: D₁ = 1, D₂ = 1, D₃ = det A = 1 − 2ρ² > 0 gives the same.)

steps.label: (a)(ii) STEP 3 · x and y  [1M]
steps.text: ⟨x, y⟩_A = xᵀAy = A₁₂ = **0** ⇒ yes, perpendicular.

steps.label: (a)(ii) STEP 4 · All z  [2M]
steps.text:
z = (z₁, z₂, z₃)
⟨x, z⟩_A = row 1 of A · z = z₁ + ρz₃ = 0 [0.5M]
⟨y, z⟩_A = row 2 of A · z = z₂ + ρz₃ = 0 [0.5M]
Put z₃ = t ⇒ **z = t(−ρ, −ρ, 1), t ∈ ℝ** [1M]

steps.label: (b)(i) STEP 5 · Jacobian  [1M]
steps.text:
f has two outputs, so ∇ₓf is a 2 × 3 matrix (one row per output):
row 1: ∇(xᵀQx)ᵀ = xᵀ(Q + Qᵀ) = **2xᵀQ** (Q symmetric)
row 2: ∇(bᵀx)ᵀ = **bᵀ**

steps.label: Where marks are lost
steps.text:
• (a) Forgetting that symmetric alone is not enough: positive definite is the condition.
• (b) Writing ∇f as one vector: f has two outputs, so it is a 2 × 3 Jacobian.
• (c) Forgetting b = c = 0.

steps.label: More
steps.text: (c) in full: [Lecture 11, Lagrangian tab](#/sem1/aiml-zc416/ch11/f-lagrange/14).
